newsitem.title: UK: UK jury told shareholders misled by hotels boss.
newsitem.headline: UK jury told shareholders misled by hotels boss.

text.p: Shareholders were misled into subscribing to a 20.6 million stg rights issue in failed British hotels group Resort Hotels by the group's chief executive, a London court was told on Monday.
"Within about two years the company was in receivership and the shares were valueless," Anthony Evans QC, representing the prosecution, told the jury at the trial of Robert Feld.
Feld denies three charges of making misleading statements to shareholders and 13 of using false instruments in 1992.
Evans said shareholders invested "a large amount of money" as a result of forged documents when they subscribed to a Resort Hotels rights issue in 1992.

He said Feld had joined his parents' hotel business in the English seaside resort of Brighton and later expanded the business by setting up a number of companies. The main one became Resort Hotels in 1985.
Evans said Feld "was essentially Resort (Hotels). If there had been no Robert Feld, there would have been no Resort."

The group was floated in 1988 and funded an expansion programme by raising millions of pounds through rights issues, issuing loan stock and large bank loans. By 1993 the group owned or managed 55 properties, ran over 3,000 rooms and employed 600 people, Evans told the court.
The case was adjourned until Tuesday. ($1=.6069 Pound)
